messages:
Alex M: Heads up — we need to shift the scheduled maintenance for model-serving nodes (Dedicated pool A) by one hour due to an unexpected firmware update window from our cloud provider. New window: 03:00–05:00 UTC on 2026-10-02. Sorry for the churn. @here :calendar:

IncidentBot: Scheduled maintenance event created: ID #mtn-20261002-02. Notifying subscribers.

Priya K: Quick q — customer impact? SLAs? Any expected 5xx spike or slow perf during the window?

Alex M: Expected impact: brief degraded throughput for small fraction of requests as we cycle nodes. No planned downtime of control plane. We expect elevated tail latency for ~3–10 minutes during rolling drains, automated fallback to smaller model variants should keep user-facing errors near zero. I'll paste an internal and customer blurb below.

Jordan L: Assigning on-call coverage: Sam (SRE) will be primary, I'll be backup for escalation. Handoff at 02:45 UTC. Sam — can you confirm runbook/readme OK? :white_check_mark: 

Sam (SRE): Confirmed. Runbook updated with the new timings. I'll be on-call and at my laptop. On my checklist:
- monitor prometheus:dedicated_pool_A.*
- watch error budget dashboard
- run smoke generator against canary route
- ready rollback: re-attach replaced nodes to old configuration

Sam (SRE): Adding the quick rollback commands here for visibility:
```
# drain node
redwood infra node drain --pool dedicated-A --node-id $NODE
# rollback model routing
redwood routing set --route canary --model-id model-v1
# force-fallback (temporary)
redwood config set fallback_model model-compact-v1
```

Priya K: Thanks. Who's on customer-facing comms? Support wants a short template they can paste.

Alex M: Support template (copy/paste):
```
Subject: Planned maintenance: brief impact possible (Oct 2, 03:00–05:00 UTC)

Hello,

We're performing scheduled maintenance on our inference nodes on Oct 2 between 03:00–05:00 UTC. During the maintenance window you may notice slightly increased response times or temporary throttling for a small subset of requests while we cycle infrastructure. There is no expected data loss and model behavior remains unchanged. If you experience errors, please reply to this message or open a ticket and reference maintenance ID mtn-20261002-02.

We appreciate your understanding,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

Jordan L: Status page draft to post at start of window (put this as a scheduled update):
```
Status: Degraded performance
Start: 2026-10-02 03:00 UTC
Impact: Some requests may see increased latency or transient throttling. No data loss expected.
Update: Engineers are performing rolling infrastructure updates and monitoring fallbacks.
```

Sam (SRE): Internal comms for Slack (support + success):
```
Hey team — scheduled maintenance active for Dedicated pool A (03:00–05:00 UTC). Expect brief latency spikes during drains. Primary on-call: Sam. Escalation: Jordan. Use incident channel #incidents for realtime updates and paste any customer reports into #support. I'll post start/complete messages and a 30m and 15m heads-up.
```

Support Bot: Reminder queued — send customer template to customers with active webhooks 30m before window.

Priya K: One more ask — can we add a note for Dedicated customers that have pinned model versions? They might notice fallback differences. Alex, can we add one line to the email? :point_up:

Alex M: Good catch. Updated support template line:
```
Note for Dedicated customers with pinned versions: we may temporarily route traffic to compatible variants during node cycling; behavior should be functionally equivalent but if you have strict exact-version constraints, open a ticket and we'll coordinate a maintenance freeze.
```

IncidentBot: Scheduled: 2026-10-02T03:00:00Z — Notification sent to subscribers who opted in.

Sam (SRE): Posting start now.

Sam (SRE): START — maintenance mtn-20261002-02 now active (03:00 UTC). Rolling drain of Dedicated pool A. Monitoring:
- dashboards: https://console.redwood/status/dedicated-A
- alerts: #ops-alerts

Alex M: I'll monitor customer replies and update the status page copy if we see anything unexpected.

Support Agent (Maya): Received one minor customer thread reporting slight slowdown at 03:04 UTC. Escalated to Sam.

Sam (SRE): Saw the spike in p95 at 03:03–03:06 UTC, no 5xx increase. Fallbacks engaged. Recovery at 03:08 UTC for that segment.

Jordan L: Nice — please keep an eye on the canary route for the next 30m.

Sam (SRE): Canary looks stable. Continuing rolling drains. Posting 30m update now.

Sam (SRE): UPDATE (03:30 UTC) — maintenance proceeding as planned. Observed transient latency in one AZ, mitigated by routing. No customer-visible errors requiring rollback. Next checkpoint in 30m.

Priya K: Any change to expected completion time?

Sam (SRE): Still on target for 05:00 UTC completion.

Support Agent (Maya): I'm pushing the support note to affected customers and linking to the status page.

IncidentBot: Automated note — scheduled maintenance progress: 50% complete.

Sam (SRE): All nodes drained in AZ-2 are back and post-update health checks OK. Moving to final AZ. ETA ~45m.

Alex M: Heads-up to sales: shared customer message sent to enterprise accounts. Sales asked for quick note they can share with execs — I pasted the one-liner in #sales-private.

Jordan L: If anything degrades, we fall back to reduced concurrency mode and extend window by controlled increments only after #exec-ops signoff.

Sam (SRE): FINAL CHECK — wrapping up. Running final smoke against critical routes.

Sam (SRE): COMPLETE — maintenance mtn-20261002-02 finished at 04:47 UTC. All pools healthy. Posting status page final update and sending customer completion note.

IncidentBot: Maintenance mtn-20261002-02 marked complete at 04:47 UTC. Subscribers notified.

Alex M: Customer completion note (copy/paste):
```
Subject: Maintenance complete — Oct 2, 04:47 UTC

Hello,

Maintenance on our inference infrastructure completed at 04:47 UTC. If you experienced any transient latency or throttling during the window, things should be back to normal now. Please reply if you're still seeing issues and include maintenance ID mtn-20261002-02.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

Support Agent (Maya): I'll close follow-up threads and mark issues as serviced. Thanks everyone.

Jordan L: Great work. Filing a short post-maint playbook note in the runbook with the AZ that had the transient latency.

Priya K: Thanks — can we add a 24h lookback on error-rate alerts to catch any delayed regressions?

Sam (SRE): Will add a follow-up ticket for 24h lookback and assign to me. :memo:

Alex M: Nicely handled — thanks team. :tada:
